patternLanded.recovered: all 3, and 3 more as a side effect of the same rule
patternLanded.generalRule: A declaration with no written type annotation whose initialiser CALLS a locally declared helper takes the helper's DECLARED RETURN TYPE. `const runtime = getSourcesWriteRuntime()` therefore resolves to `SourcesWriteRuntime | undefined` -> `SourcesWriteRuntime`, and `runtime.productService` resolves through the runtime shape to the Port the boundary implements.
patternLanded.whyItWasInvisible: The helper's return type is written on the ARROW SIGNATURE, which the declaration index carries in the initialiser text (`(): SourcesWriteRuntime | undefined => activeRuntime`), never in the annotation field. Reading only type annotations finds nothing.
patternLanded.additionalDefectFixedAlongside: a type annotation of the form `A | B` or `Pick<A,'x'>` reduced to no type name at all; the union alternative and the generic type argument are now both considered.

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: the body walk started at the function's Block, and a function's parameter list is a sibling of that Block, not a child — so no injected dependency declared as a parameter was ever visible to the calls in the body
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.impact: GENERAL and large: production dependencies arrive as parameters far more often than as locals. `registerAISettingsRoutes(..., semanticCorpusSourceSnapshotReader?: Pick<...>)` is the canonical shape.
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — the walk now starts at the function-like scope (parameters + body) and descends into nested function-likes as their own scope

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.defect: a call site nested in a callback was attributed to EVERY enclosing body, and deduplication let whichever context the index reached first decide
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: an outer body cannot see a nested function's locals, so it reports the same site as `unresolved`; keeping the first record made reachability depend on traversal ORDER
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.impact: general — this defect was introduced by the R-6 fix and is recorded here because it was found by the mandated regression check, not by inspection
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — each call site is owned by the context that RESOLVES its receiver, falling back to the deepest context. Verified: 0 boundaries changed verdict as a result.

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.defect: type-alias constituents were extracted with a text scan that (a) missed `Pick<Port, ...>` entirely, (b) admitted METHOD NAMES as if they were type names, and (c) treated nested type references without regard to nesting
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: `X = Pick<A,'a'> & Pick<A,'b'>` reduced to the literal string `appendEpistemicReentryTrigger`
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.impact: GENERAL in both directions: real Port bindings looked like collisions, and admitting `saveRevision` as a 'constituent' linked two unrelated repository Ports that merely declare it, which turned a real caller into an ambiguity
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — aliases are now walked as a type tree; only type references count, member-level references do not, and a utility applied to a type contributes that type argument

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: a class implementing a broad Port was not registered as an implementation of the NARROWING alias derived from it (`DiscoveryFeedbackWriteRepositoryPort = Pick<DiscoveryFeedbackRepositoryPort, ...>`), so the narrow Port looked like it had no production implementation
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — the index closes over the alias graph in both directions, one hop per narrowing alias (NOT transitively: two sibling narrowings of one Port are unrelated, and closing them would create false ambiguity)

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.defect: QUALIFICATION WAS EXPRESSED TWICE AND THE TWO COPIES DISAGREED
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: `resolveReachability` accepted any receiver the alias/Port rule matched, while the caller-classification rule accepted only a literal class name or a single-implementation Port. `ProductFindingRepository = DiscoveryFindingRepositoryPort & DiscoveryFindingLifecycleRepositoryPort` and `SemanticGenerationRepository = SemanticIndexRepositoryPort & SemanticGenerationLifecycleRepositoryPort` were therefore accepted as callers and then classified as collisions.
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.impact: general — it hid every composite-Port listener of a boundary that has no `implements` clause naming the composite
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — `boundaryMatchKind()` is now the single expression of the doctrine and `resolveReachability` delegates to it, so the verdict and the classification cannot disagree

resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.defect: object-literal FACTORIES were not implementations of the Port they satisfy
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.cause: nothing records that `(pool: Pool): ActivityReadModelStorePort => ({ ..., async commitProjectProjection() {} })` binds its literal to that Port, because no class implements it
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.impact: general — every module-level boundary whose closure satisfies a Port looked unreachable, and every builder holding that Port looked like a name collision
resolverDefectsFixedThisRound.status: FIXED — a factory whose declared return type is a Port and whose returned literal provides the method counts as an implementation of that Port

sourceVerifiedCollisions.proof: Every same-named call site has receiver type `DiscoveryTriggerRuntimeRepositoryPort` (modules/discovery-trigger-coordinator/src/index.ts:66). The ONLY class in the repository that implements that Port is `InMemoryDiscoveryRuntimeRepository` (adapters/discovery-trigger-coordinator/src/index.ts:631) — an in-memory stand-in. `PostgresDiscoveryRuntimeRepository` (adapters/discovery-runtime-postgres/src/index.ts) implements `DiscoveryRuntimeExecutionRepositoryPort` and `DiscoveryActivityReadPort`, and the Port is offered only as an optional injection point (`readonly discoveryRuntimeRepository?: ...`, server.ts:817) with no durable binder anywhere in the composition root.
sourceVerifiedCollisions.conclusion: the call reaches a DIFFERENT repository contract; it cannot reach this boundary. Genuine method-name collision.

sourceVerifiedCollisions.proof: same single call site family and the same Port as saveJob (modules/discovery-trigger-coordinator/src/index.ts:738)
sourceVerifiedCollisions.conclusion: genuine method-name collision, same evidence as saveJob

sourceVerifiedCollisions.proof: 8 same-named call sites, every one on an UNRELATED Port: TransformationRepositoryPort (x2), ProjectAIConfigurationPort, StandingAIProcessingPolicyWriterPort, ChangeSetReviewRepositoryPort (x2), DiscoveryReviewResourceWriterPort, IntakeRepositoryPort, plus 1 unresolved. The composite the boundary IS wired through is `type ProductFindingRepository = DiscoveryFindingRepositoryPort & DiscoveryFindingLifecycleRepositoryPort` (adapters/discovery-runtime-product/src/index.ts). Enumerating EVERY member access on that composite in that file shows listByProject, findLifecycle, saveFenced, findRevision, listByProjectPage — `save` is never called on it.
sourceVerifiedCollisions.conclusion: no call site reaches this boundary. Genuine method-name collision.

doctrineRulingRequired.resolverVerdict: PROVEN (SOLE — the receiver type `AuthRepositoryPort` has one production implementation, the boundary)
doctrineRulingRequired.sourceFact: the single call site (assemblies/shotgun-app/src/server.ts:2553) is inside `if (testDevelopmentAuth)`, and `testDevelopmentAuth = process.env.VITEST === 'true' && !options.authRepository && !production` (server.ts:2549-2550). Under `NODE_ENV=production` the guard is FALSE.
doctrineRulingRequired.theQuestion: Does a production-reachability authority that reads STATIC wiring treat a call behind a runtime configuration guard as production reachable?
doctrineRulingRequired.whyItIsNotASimpleCollision: unlike the three above, the receiver type genuinely IS the boundary's Port and the boundary genuinely IS its only implementation. The call is eligible on the production code path and suppressed by deployment configuration — the same SHAPE of question as `PostgresConnectorRuntimeState.recoverExpiredLeases`, which the owner already ruled to be production reachable.
doctrineRulingRequired.bothOutcomesKeepREVIEW_REQUIREDZero: PROVEN (guard is not part of static reachability, consistent with the recoverExpiredLeases ruling) or TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD (a VITEST-gated call is test evidence). Neither requires a rule change; the ruling only decides which of the two statuses is recorded.
doctrineRulingRequired.recommendation: PROVEN, for consistency with the recoverExpiredLeases ruling: static wiring is the authority, and a configuration guard is recorded as evidence rather than as unreachability. This round did NOT change it.
